record.paper_title: Extra extension properties of equidimensional holomorphic mappings: results and open questions
record.context_brief: Extension of punctured-ball maps to compact Kähler surfaces
record.original_question: Let X be a compact Kähler surface, let B* = B \ {0} be the punctured ball, and let f: B* → X be a locally biholomorphic mapping. Suppose f extends meromorphically to the whole ball B, and let E := f̂[0] be the full image of the origin under this meromorphic extension. Prove that E is an exceptional curve in X.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $B \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ (with $n \ge 2$) denote the open unit ball, and let $B^* = B \setminus \{0\}$ be the punctured ball. Let $X$ be a compact Kähler surface, and let $f : B^* \to X$ be a locally biholomorphic holomorphic mapping. It is known that under these hypotheses $f$ extends to a meromorphic mapping $\hat{f} : B \dashrightarrow X$ on the entire ball. Define the full image of the origin under this meromorphic extension by
$$E := \hat{f}[0],$$
i.e., the set of all limits $\lim_{k\to\infty} f(z_k)$ taken over sequences $z_k \in B^*$ with $z_k \to 0$ for which the limit exists in $X$ (equivalently, the fiber over $0$ of the graph of $\hat{f}$, projected to $X$).

Recall that an irreducible compact curve $C$ in a complex surface $X$ is called exceptional if it can be contracted to a point in some smooth complex surface, i.e., there exists a proper bimeromorphic morphism $\pi : X \to X'$ onto a (possibly singular) complex surface that maps $C$ to a single point and is biholomorphic on $X \setminus C$. A compact analytic subset of $X$ is called an exceptional curve if it is a finite union of irreducible exceptional curves contractible (simultaneously) to a point.

Prove that $E$ is an exceptional curve in $X$, or produce a counterexample.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not surface a published proof or counterexample to this specific question about the full image of the origin being an exceptional curve under meromorphic extension of locally biholomorphic punctured-ball maps into compact Kähler surfaces. Related work by Ivashkovich on meromorphic extension theorems is cited in subsequent literature (e.g., papers on non-algebraizable neighborhoods of curves), but no source clearly states this question has been resolved.

status_evidence.title: Non-algebraizable neighborhoods of curves
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions based on an extension theorem of S. Ivashkovich, patching neighborhoods of curves in projective surfaces and blowing down exceptional curves.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work cites Ivashkovich's extension theorem framework but does not record this specific question as resolved.

status_evidence.title: One example in concern with extension and separate analyticity properties of meromorphic mappings
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of a non-Kähler compact 3-fold showing limits of meromorphic extension; obstructions described via Lelong numbers.
status_evidence.claim: Related counterexamples exist in the non-Kähler 3-fold setting but do not address the compact Kähler surface case posed here.
